report.summary: Analyzed harness.py chunk 1 of 4. Verified docstring claims against code. Found 2 broken claims (NEVER RAISES, fail-closed focus gate) and 1 uncheckable claim (Tier 2 never crashes Tier 1). No redundant checks or inverted rules.
risks: eval_task_tier1 | medium | NEVER RAISES claim broken: task['repo'] unguarded subscript raises KeyError | Add try/except around task['repo'] or verify claim
_is_focus_withheld | medium | fail-closed claim broken: does not check role=="focus" case-insensitively | Add case-insensitive check or verify slice.py always uses lowercase

claims.why: Tier 2 code not in this chunk; cannot verify it never raises unhandled exceptions in Tier 1 context

claims.text: Tier 2 NEVER makes a network call unless explicitly enabled
claims.why: Tier 2 implementation not in this chunk; cannot verify network call gating

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: a resolution failure ... is caught and returned as an ERRORED row instead of propagating
claims.why: Line 125: task['repo'] is an unguarded subscript that raises KeyError if 'repo' missing; not caught by (ValueError, OSError) handler. Also task['target'] on same line also unguarded.

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is refused here before anything is sliced
claims.why: Line 117-118: calls is_correctness_task(task) and returns _correctness_task_row(task) before any slicing

claims.text: Aggregated PER LABEL-PROVENANCE TIER ... never blended into one number
claims.why: Lines 74-77: _by_provenance and _group_rows_by_provenance ensure aggregation only within (provenance, tier) buckets; no top-level blended mean exists in this chunk

claims.text: tier == 'quarantine' tasks are excluded from every headline and reported separately
claims.why: Lines 63-64: _is_primary_tier returns False for non-'primary' tiers; quarantine tasks are grouped separately in _group_rows_by_provenance

claims.text: Any task with recall < 1.0 is a *slice-recall miss*; we surface exactly which symbols were dropped
claims.why: Lines 139-140: missed list included in eval_task_tier1 return; _tier1_aggregate counts misses and lists missed_ids

claims.text: Fail-closed: only the EXACT string 'primary' counts. A missing, typo'd, or otherwise unrecognized tier is treated as quarantine
Both tier buckets always exist (possibly empty)
claims.why: Lines 59-60: out[prov] = {'primary': [], 'quarantine': []} before any row assignment

claims.text: CALLERS MUST PRE-FILTER OUT ERRORED ROWS AND FOCUS-WITHHELD ROWS before passing rows here
claims.why: Docstring states the requirement; code does not filter itself

claims.text: ABSENT, not None ... any aggregation path that forgets to filter on error fails loudly (KeyError)
claims.why: Returned dict has 'error' key but no 'recall' or 'compression' keys

claims.text: Refused as an ERRORED row ... excluded from all aggregates
claims.why: Returns _task_error_row with 'error' key; no recall/compression keys

claims.text: the withheld block contains a role=="focus" entry -- the exact shape slice.py emits when the unconditional secret floor fires on the target itself
claims.why: Line 99: checks w.get('role') == 'focus'; docstring claims case-insensitive 'role=="focus"' but code uses exact string compare. If slice.py ever emits 'Focus' or 'FOCUS', this would return False, breaking the fail-closed claim.

claims.text: ABSENT, not a zero -- same 'any aggregator that forgets to filter fails loudly' contract as the error marker
claims.why: Returned dict has 'focus_withheld' key but no recall/compression keys

observations.what: eval_task_tier1 does not guard task['repo'] and task['target'] subscript access, breaking 'NEVER RAISES' claim
_is_focus_withheld uses exact string compare for role, but docstring implies case-insensitive match; if slice.py ever uses different casing, fail-closed property fails
